column47: The American Studies Program at Purdue University is one of the oldest in the country, but our approach is decidedly contemporary. At Purdue, American Studies is an interdisciplinary program that draws on more than 100 faculty from across the university. column2: Graduate Certificate in Healthcare Quality Improvement
column16: To be considered for admission to the Graduate Certificate in Healthcare Quality Improvement, applicants must submit the following: A completed online application. A statement of purpose (approximately 500 words). A current resume. Three letters of recommendation. Official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended. A bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution with a minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale.
column47: The Healthcare Quality Improvement Graduate Certificate program prepares nurses and other healthcare professionals to work in interprofessional teams to improve the quality of healthcare and patient outcomes. Using an evidence-based practice framework, students will learn to apply the basic and advanced principles and methods of quality improvement to health systems. Students will gain the skills to perform data analysis and identify and lead initiatives that improve care, reduce costs, and maximize efficiency. Coursework focuses on the core principles of quality and safety in healthcare, data management, and lean and six-sigma methods for health systems.

column2: Graduate Certificate in Managing Information Technology Projects
column16: To be eligible for this certificate program, you must have an undergraduate degree from an accredited university with a 3.0 or higher GPA. Admission requires a completed online application, current resume, statement of purpose (500 words), and one set of official transcripts.
column47: Effective project management is the cornerstone of success for any organization. This 12-credit-hour certificate program is designed to provide you with the essential skills and knowledge needed to excel in the complex world of information technology project management. In this program, you will learn to navigate the intricacies of planning, executing, and closing IT projects, ensuring they are completed on time, within budget, and to the highest quality standards. You will explore critical concepts such as project scope, risk management, stakeholder engagement, and team leadership, all tailored specifically to the unique challenges of the IT landscape.

column2: Graduate Certificate in Systems
column16: Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution with a 3.0 GPA or better. Applicants with a 3.0 GPA from a non-accredited institution or a GPA below 3.0 will be considered on a case-by-case basis. The application requires: Undergraduate transcripts, Resume, Statement of Purpose, three letters of recommendation.
column47: Engineers today must navigate a world of ever-increasing complexity. The Graduate Certificate in Systems provides the conceptual and practical tools you need to model, design and manage complex systems throughout their life cycle. These tools include systems thinking, systems modeling and analysis, and systems architecting and management. In just three courses, you can learn the fundamentals of systems and gain specialized knowledge in your field. Gain a systems perspective on complex problems. Build a systems engineering toolkit that includes modeling, architecting, and management. Enhance your existing expertise in a discipline like mechanical, electrical, or industrial engineering with the ability to see the 'big picture.' Learn to manage projects that involve multiple disciplines and components.

column2: Post-Master's Certificate in Adult Gerontology Primary Care
column16: Applicants must have earned a Master of Science in Nursing (MSN) from a CCNE or ACEN accredited program. A minimum grade point average of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale is required for admission. Applicants must hold a current, unencumbered RN license in the United States. Application documents include three letters of recommendation, official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions, a statement of purpose, and a professional resume or CV.
column46: Adult Gerontology Primary Care Nurse Practitioner
column47: The Post-Master’s certificate program is designed for students who already have a master’s degree in nursing and want to pursue a new specialty. The program of study is individualized based on the student’s previous coursework and clinical experience. Upon completion of the program, students are eligible to sit for national certification in their chosen specialty. Adult-Gerontology Primary Care Nurse Practitioners provide primary care to patients from age 13 through the end of life. They focus on health promotion, disease prevention, and management of acute and chronic health conditions in a variety of primary care settings.
